## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Aggikabhāradvājajātaka* (Ja 129) is a narrative included in the Jātaka collection of the Pali canon. Set at Jetavana near Sāvatthī, the frame story relates that the Buddha told the account concerning another hypocrite, opening with the verse line: "’Twas greed".

In early European scholarship, particularly in V. Fausbøll's edition of the Jātaka, the text is titled *Aggika Jātaka* [Ray 1946]. Niharranjan Ray observes that while Fausbøll's edition adopts the title *Aggika Jātaka*, Burmese epigraphical records and temple representations—such as those depicting the complete series of Jātakas in Pagan—preserve the name *Aggikabhāradvāja Jātaka* [Ray 1946].
